overview: Align mobile and desktop (PC agent) UI/behavior, fix agent/device naming, stabilize terminal session sync and control, add terminal notifications to mobile, enforce fixed ports, and harden error handling without breaking existing pairing flows.
goals: Unify button labels and behaviors across mobile and desktop so same-named actions do the same thing
Show PC agent identity using host name or device ID instead of IP:port
Keep terminal session lists consistent across mobile and desktop with rename support and operability
Forward terminal notifications from desktop agent to mobile and surface them in timeline/alerts
Guarantee QR pairing and static token + addr login are both supported with approval + token reuse
Enforce configured ports for local server and ROI QUIC, with clear startup errors on conflict
Provide friendly, actionable errors with developer-facing details across both clients
nonGoals: Do not add automatic port-fallback or random port selection
Do not add auto-discovery or new cloud relay services
Do not redesign the entire UI; only align and harden the existing experience
Do not change the core auth model (tokens + pairing)
successMetrics: QR pairing and static token + addr login both succeed end-to-end with clear errors on failure
Agent label never shows raw IP:port when host name or device ID is available
Terminal session list is non-empty when sessions exist and reconciles within one refresh cycle
Terminal session rename appears on both mobile and desktop within 5 seconds
Device list shows mobile device name + device ID and supports unbind/offline actions
Port conflicts block startup with an explicit error message and no fallback
openQuestions: Should terminal session metadata persist across desktop agent restarts, or should sessions be marked closed with a clear reason?
What exact device name should mobile report (platform-only vs model name) if OS APIs allow?
What is the source of terminal notifications (command completion, explicit 'notify' command, or error-only)?
Do we need desktop-side test/lint/build commands as quality gates in addition to mobile?
Where should desktop store new metadata (extend identity JSON vs a new storage file)?

stack.database: Mobile: SQLite via sqflite; Desktop: JSON file(s) on disk
stack.auth: QR pairing with approval + device-bound long-lived token + static tokens

routes.purpose: QR, device list, terminal sessions, status

routes.purpose: Scan pairing QR and approve flow

uiNotes: Button labels must match behavior across mobile and desktop; create a single action map and align naming
Agent display name priority: user-defined label > host_name > device_id > short token; never raw IP:port when host_name/device_id exists
Device list shows '<device name> · <device id>' with status tags and clear actions (Disconnect vs Unbind vs Block)
Terminal sessions show label, status, last activity, last output preview, and allow rename + open detail
Errors show friendly summary with expandable developer details (error code, endpoint, request id)
Empty states differentiate 'no sessions' from 'cannot fetch sessions'
rules: Desktop agent must bind to configured listen_port and roi_quic_port only; if unavailable, startup fails with an explicit error and no fallback
QR pairing requires approval and returns a device-bound token reused for the same client_id; static token + addr login must bypass approval
Agent display name must never default to raw IP:port if host_name or device_id is available
Device names shown on desktop must include mobile device name + device ID, and unbind must revoke the device-bound token
Terminal session rename must be validated (non-empty, length-limited) and synchronized to both ends; if sync fails, revert and show error
Terminal session list reconciliation uses desktop as source of truth for running sessions; missing sessions are marked closed with a reason
Terminal notifications are deduplicated and rate-limited per session to avoid spam
Error surfaces include user-friendly summaries plus developer diagnostics (code, request id, endpoint)

stories.title: Define and enforce UI action parity across mobile and desktop
stories.description: As a user, I want the same-named buttons on mobile and desktop to perform the same actions so the UI is predictable.
acceptanceCriteria: Create an action-parity map (document or config) listing each shared action name and its expected behavior
Update mobile and desktop UI labels and handlers to match the action-parity map
Example: a button labeled 'Disconnect' removes the active session but keeps the pairing on both platforms
Negative case: a mismatched label/action is detected (manual QA checklist) and corrected before release

stories.title: Expose host_name from desktop identity and use it for agent display
stories.description: As a user, I want the PC agent to be identified by host name or device ID rather than IP:port.
acceptanceCriteria: Desktop identity response includes host_name (and is stored in pairing status as needed)
Mobile stores host_name and uses it in agent display label priority
Example: after QR pairing, the agent label shows 'MyMacBook' instead of '192.168.1.10:8899'
Negative case: if host_name is missing, the label falls back to device_id instead of IP:port

stories.title: Show mobile device name + device ID in desktop device list
stories.description: As a desktop user, I want connected devices to show a clear mobile device name and device ID so I can manage them.
acceptanceCriteria: Mobile sends a device name plus device ID (client_id) for client_name or a new dedicated field
Desktop device list displays '<device name> · <device id>' and keeps existing actions (block/kick/forget)
Example: device appears as 'iOS · 8f3a1b' with last seen time
Negative case: if device name is empty, desktop shows 'Unknown · <device id>' and still allows unbind

stories.title: Add terminal session labels and rename synchronization
stories.description: As a user, I want to rename terminal sessions and have the name synced between mobile and desktop.
acceptanceCriteria: Terminal session payloads include a label field in list/status responses
Add a terminal rename action that updates desktop session metadata and syncs to mobile storage
Example: rename session to 'Deploy logs' on mobile and the desktop list shows the same label within 5 seconds
Negative case: renaming to an empty string is rejected with a user-friendly error and no changes applied

stories.title: Fix terminal session list reconciliation and persistence
stories.description: As a user, I want terminal session lists to stay consistent across reconnects and not appear empty when sessions exist.
acceptanceCriteria: Desktop provides a stable list of running/recent terminal sessions; mobile reconciles with local storage
Mobile differentiates 'no sessions' from 'cannot fetch sessions' with distinct UI states
Example: after reconnect, sessions created earlier appear in both mobile and desktop lists
Negative case: if the desktop agent restarted and sessions are gone, mobile marks them as closed with a clear reason

stories.title: Enable terminal session operation from desktop UI
stories.description: As a desktop user, I want to open a terminal session and interact with it directly from the desktop UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Desktop UI provides a terminal session detail view with live output and input support (WebSocket or polling)
Desktop UI supports resize and stop actions consistent with mobile behavior
Example: open a session, run 'ls', and see output update live
Negative case: if the session is missing or ended, the UI shows a non-blocking error and disables input

stories.title: Forward terminal notifications from desktop to mobile
stories.description: As a mobile user, I want terminal notifications received by the desktop agent to appear on mobile.
acceptanceCriteria: Define a terminal notification payload and delivery path from desktop agent to mobile
Mobile stores notifications in timeline and optionally surfaces a toast/banner
Example: terminal session emits a warning notification and mobile shows it in the timeline
Negative case: if mobile is offline, notifications queue or fail gracefully without crashing

stories.title: Harden pairing flows for QR approval + static token + addr
stories.description: As a user, I want both QR pairing (with approval) and static token + addr login to work reliably with clear errors.
acceptanceCriteria: QR pairing flow validates expiry, requires approval, and stores the device-bound token on success
Manual login accepts static token + addr without requiring desktop approval when token is valid
Example: scan QR, approve on desktop, and reconnect later using stored token without re-approval
Negative case: expired QR shows an explicit error and prompts to generate a new code

stories.title: Enforce fixed ports for local server and ROI QUIC
stories.description: As an operator, I want the desktop agent to fail fast on port conflicts instead of switching ports.
acceptanceCriteria: Desktop agent refuses to start if listen_port or roi_quic_port is in use and reports the conflict
UI surfaces a clear error message with the conflicting port number and remediation hint
Example: port 8899 in use -> startup error shown in UI and logs
Negative case: the agent does not auto-select another port or start silently

stories.title: Standardize error handling and diagnostics across clients
stories.description: As a user and developer, I want errors to be friendly yet actionable with diagnostic details.
acceptanceCriteria: All major connection/terminal/device errors map to user-friendly messages and structured error codes
Developer details (code, endpoint, request id) are available via UI expansion or logs
Example: invalid token shows a friendly message and error code 'invalid_token'
Negative case: raw stack traces or empty error dialogs are not shown to users
